name: Cagliari
title: Cagliari Ship Thickness Gauging | UTM for Tankers and Ferries
description: Ultrasonic thickness gauging at Cagliari, Sardinia, for tankers, container feeders, ro-pax ferries and cargo ships: hull, tank and piping measurement.
h1: Ship Hull and Tank Thickness Measurement at Cagliari, Sardinia
intro: Cagliari is the main port of southern Sardinia, set on a wide gulf with a canal port for containers, ferry quays near the old town and industrial berths along the shore. The Sarroch refinery lies a short distance to the south-west. Owners gauge tankers, feeders, ferries and cargo ships here before dockings and at charter changes. Atlantis NDT sends a thickness measurement team from India to the ship, and plans work around cargo, ferry rotations and the anchorage.

highlights.p: Product tankers and crude carriers working the refinery to the south-west often wait or lie at anchor in the gulf, which creates windows to gauge ballast tanks and deck steel before or after cargo work.

highlights.h: Feeder ships on tight container rotations
highlights.p: Container feeders at the canal port have short, predictable stays, so gauging focuses on ballast tanks, hatch coamings and accessible hull structure that a cargo plan leaves open.
Ferries linking Sardinia with Sicily and the mainland call on fixed schedules, allowing vehicle decks, ramps and tanks to be gauged in stages ahead of a docking.

port.h: The port of Cagliari: gulf anchorage, canal port and ferry quays
p: Cagliari lies at the head of a broad gulf on the south coast of Sardinia, with the old town rising behind the harbour. The Gulf of Cagliari gives wide, open anchorage for ships waiting for berths or between cargoes, though it is exposed to southerly weather. The port has several distinct areas: the historic port near the centre for ferries and cruise ships, an industrial port serving bulk and petroleum cargoes, and the canal port, a dedicated container terminal on the western side that handles feeder ships and some transshipment traffic.

Traffic mixes the island's own needs with wider Mediterranean flows. Ferries and ro-pax ships link Cagliari with mainland Italy and Sicily, carrying vehicles, freight trailers and passengers. Container feeders call at the canal port, and bulk carriers and general cargo ships bring in and take out materials for island industry. Tankers serve the refinery at Sarroch and other energy facilities along the coast. Cruise ships call throughout the warmer part of the year, and workboats and tugs support all of it. The variety of ship types means that almost any survey need can arise here.

Weather and season shape inspection planning. Summer brings busier ferry timetables and more cruise calls, limiting how long a passenger ship can be taken out of rotation. Cooler months are better for ferries, when schedules ease. Southerly winds can raise swell in the gulf and make launch work at the anchorage harder, so owners often prefer berth work when they need dependable access. Tankers waiting for a refinery berth may spend longer at anchor than expected, which can open a window for gauging if the weather cooperates and the ship has gas-free certificates.

facilities.h: Where gauging can happen at Cagliari
p: Cagliari has ship repair activity in the historic port, with repair quays and floating dock capacity suited to coasters, ferries, tugs and mid-sized cargo ships. Larger tonnage usually docks elsewhere in Italy, in Malta or further afield, and Cagliari then acts as the measuring point before the voyage to the yard. A ship brought into a dock or onto a repair quay offers access to the lower hull, sea chests, rudder and propeller, and to double-bottom and tank structure after cleaning.

Away from the repair quays, gauging takes place alongside at the ferry berths, the canal port, the industrial berths and the anchorage. Feeder ships are gauged on their hatch coamings, hatch covers, ballast tanks and accessible hull structure while the cargo plan allows. Ferries offer vehicle decks and ramps between sailings. Tankers at industrial berths or at anchor offer ballast tanks, deck steel and piping when the terminal and the master agree. Lay-up and idle periods give the longest windows for a full programme.
list: Historic port repair quays and floating dock capacity: bottom shell, sea chests and tank structure of ferries, coasters, tugs and mid-sized ships
Canal port container berths: hatch coamings, ballast tanks and accessible hull structure of feeder ships between cargo operations
Ferry berths: vehicle decks, ramps and tanks of ro-pax ships on island rotations
Industrial and petroleum berths: ballast tanks, deck plating and cargo piping of tankers, subject to terminal permits
Gulf of Cagliari anchorage: ships waiting or between cargoes, reached by launch in settled weather
Porto Torres and Palermo: other yards and ports used for larger dockings after gauging

context.h: Port state control and Sardinian shipping regulation
p: Port state control at Cagliari is carried out by the Italian Coast Guard (Guardia Costiera) through the harbour master (Capitaneria di Porto), under the Paris MoU system. Ports in Sardinia fall under the Sardinian Sea port authority, which also oversees other island harbours. Tankers, bulk carriers and older general cargo ships are all candidates for inspection, and structural deficiencies can be a reason for detention, so owners benefit from knowing thickness condition before a ship arrives.

The EU Ship Recycling Regulation requires an Inventory of Hazardous Materials for ships calling at EU ports, and a docking is the practical time to survey and update it. EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime now influence how long owners keep older ferries and cargo ships trading. Container feeders and tankers surveyed under class rules need thickness reports in the formats the societies expect, and gauging in Cagliari before a docking keeps the surveyor's time at the yard focused on close-up work and repairs.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs at Cagliari
jobs.p: Cagliari work covers a broad range of ships, from feeder vessels on regular loops to tankers and ferries. Each job starts with a defined list of spaces, agreed with the superintendent, and a plan that fits the berth and cargo schedule. We record readings by structural member, compare them with earlier survey data when the owner can supply it, and deliver one report for the owner and the yard.
list: Hatch coaming and ballast tank gauging on a container feeder at the canal port between rotations
Pre-docking gauging of a ro-pax ferry's vehicle decks, ramps and tanks ahead of a yard period
Owner's condition gauging of a product tanker lying at anchor in the gulf before a change of charter
Bottom shell and sea chest gauging on a coaster or tug hauled out on a repair quay or floating dock
Scrubber wash-water piping thickness checks on a ferry or cruise ship during a layover

logistics: Cagliari Elmas airport lies close to the city and port, with direct links to mainland Italy and several European cities, which keeps the transfer short once the team lands. The crew travels from India on Schengen visas, so dates are fixed after allowing for visa processing. The ship's agent arranges port and terminal access, and we send crew details and an equipment list ahead of time so passes are ready.

faqs.q: Can a container feeder be gauged at the Cagliari canal port?
faqs.a: Yes, between cargo operations and with the agreement of the terminal. The usual scope is hatch coamings, hatch covers, ballast tanks and any hull structure accessible from inside. Feeder stays are short, so we agree the target list with the superintendent in advance and keep the readings in a single report.

faqs.q: Is there a repair yard in Cagliari for steel renewal?
faqs.a: There are repair quays and floating dock capacity suited to smaller and mid-sized ships. Larger tonnage generally docks elsewhere in Italy, in Malta or further afield. Gauging in Cagliari gives the owner an early thickness record so the steel estimate is ready before a ship reaches the yard.

faqs.q: Can tankers waiting for Sarroch be gauged at the anchorage?
faqs.a: Often, in settled weather and when the ship has made its spaces safe. We reach the ship by launch, and the master confirms gas-free certificates and the entry permit. A southerly swell can stop the work, so it helps to hold a spare day in the plan, and the time at anchor is frequently the longest window.

faqs.q: What can be gauged on a ferry between island sailings?
faqs.a: Typically vehicle deck sections, ramps and their supporting structure, and ballast tanks the crew can ventilate. Several calls can add up to a full programme. We agree the sequence with the superintendent so each visit has a clear target and the readings come together in one report.
